wrapper_defects_corrected.defect_1_response_metadata_source: v1 read result.finish_reason / result.prompt_tokens; the REAL provider exposes these under result.wire_observation (src/sse-accumulator.ts WireObservation). v2 reads wire_observation first with top-level fallbacks for scripted providers. Qualification C: a scripted result carrying wire_observation {finish_reason:'tool_use', prompt_tokens:4321} yields a response record with exactly those values.
wrapper_defects_corrected.defect_2_failed_requests_not_archived: v1 captured only after a successful provider return. v2 writes a REQUEST record BEFORE forwarding and pairs it with a RESPONSE record on success or an ERROR record (same request_id, verbatim error message) on throw; the provider error propagates. Qualification E: a provider 503 produces request+error records sharing the request_id and rethrows.
wrapper_defects_corrected.defect_3_capability_preservation: v1 object-spread ({...inner}) dropped prototype methods (e.g. completeStructured). v2 is a Proxy over the inner provider: only complete/completeMultiTurn are overridden; every other property resolves on the inner provider with its ORIGINAL function reference and this-binding (the real class uses TS-private regular properties, not #private fields, so proxy receivers are safe). Qualification F: the REAL provider built by the same resolveLLMProvider call the live driver uses (DynamicLLMProvider — members complete, getProvider, setProvider, syncMultiTurnCapability) is enumerated: all preserved by reference, 0 lost, behavioral probe (setProvider/syncMultiTurnCapability/getProvider through the proxy) executes; completeStructured identity additionally proven on the prototype-method harness class (the openai_compatible multi-turn provider does not declare it at 9f298f2 — it lives on the opt-in structured subclass; the guarantee is conditional-preservation).

fail_closed_policy: ANY capture-write failure throws a 'wire-capture: …' error. On the REQUEST phase this happens BEFORE the model call — no unaudited traffic can leave; the resulting workflow failure is an ordinary infra-class failure under the preregistered taxonomy. On the RESPONSE phase (the call already happened) the error propagates and the loop's existing handling applies; the request record still proves the call was audited. Qualification D: construction-phase (uncreatable location) and append-phase (read-only capture directory) failures both throw the marker with ZERO inner-provider invocations.
live_driver_integration: the driver (campaign tooling, untracked, outside the frozen implementation) imports this same wrapper module and wraps the resolved provider at stack construction (journal event provider_resolved records the capture path); qualification F constructs the real provider exactly the way the driver does.
